L0: ---
L1: name: winui-ui-testing
L2: description: "Automated UI testing for Windows desktop apps — generate a batch test script with the `winapp ui` UI Automation harness (WinApp CLI 0.7+), run all tests in one pass, read results. Covers assertions, interactions, keyboard/touch/pen input, file pickers, dialogs, persistence, accessibility, and screenshot/video capture for Win32, WPF, WinForms, and WinUI 3, in Windows Sandbox or locally."
L3: ---
L4: ### Scope and execution boundary
L5: 
L6: `winapp ui` uses Windows UI Automation (UIA), so the AutomationId-based workflow works with any Windows desktop framework, packaged or unpackaged. Skip WinUI-specific binding/dialog advice for other frameworks.
L7: Windows Sandbox keeps synthetic input off the user's desktop; target selection is in Step 1. Discover the installed contract with `winapp run --help`, `winapp target --help`, and `winapp ui <verb> --help`. Use `--on sandbox`, not `--sandbox` or a top-level `sandbox` command. Do not enable Windows features or launch an app without the task's permission.
L8: - Prerequisites and enablement: see `winui-setup`.
L9: - Project builds/publishes execute on the **host**; deployment, app launch, and `ui --on sandbox` execute in the **guest**. Run the batch script below on the host, not inside `target exec` (which would double-route).
L10: - Real input and capture require an unlocked host and a connected, nonminimized Sandbox client. Tree inspection may work while input cannot; a readable tree is not an input-readiness check.

L102: If a repository does not exist, restic (since 0.17.0) will return exit code `10` and print a corresponding error message. Older versions return exit code `1`. Note that restic will also return exit code `1` if a different error is encountered (e.g.: incorrect password to `cat config`) and it may print a different error message. If there are no errors, restic will return a zero exit code and print the repository metadata.
L103: ## Exit codes【5†】
L104: 
L105: Restic commands return an exit code that signals whether the command was successful. The following table provides a general description, see the help of each command for a more specific description.
L106: 
L107: Warning

L112: 2  | Go runtime error
L113: 3  | `backup` could not read some source data, or `forget` could not remove one or more snapshots
L114: 10  | Repository does not exist (since restic 0.17.0)
L115: 11  | Failed to lock repository (since restic 0.17.0)
L116: 12  | Wrong password (since restic 0.17.1)

L128: ### Exit errors【7†】
L129: 
L130: Fatal errors will result in a final JSON message on `stderr` before the process exits. It will hold the error message and the exit code.
L131: 
L132: Note
L133: 
L134: Some errors cannot be caught and reported this way, such as Go runtime errors or command line parsing errors.

L139: ### Output formats【8†】
L140: 
L141: Commands print their main JSON output on `stdout`. The generated JSON output uses one of the following two formats.
L142: 
L143: Note
L144: 
L145: Not all messages and errors have been converted to JSON yet. Feel free to submit a pull request!
L146: 
L147: The datatypes specified in the following sections roughly correspond to the underlying Go types and are mapped to the JSON types as follows:
L148: 
L149:   * `int32`, `int64`, `uint32`, `uint64` and `float64` are encoded as number.
L150:   * `bool` and `string` correspond to the respective types.
L151: 
L152:   * `[]` in front of a type indicates that the field is an array of the respective type.
L153: 
L154:   * `time.Time` is encoded as a string in RFC3339 format.
L155: 
L156:   * `os.FileMode` is encoded as an `uint32`.
L157: 
L158: If a field contains a default value like `0` or `""`, it may be omitted from the JSON output.
L159: #### Single JSON document【9†】
L160: 
L161: Several commands output a single JSON document that can be parsed in its entirety. Depending on the command, the output consists of either a single or multiple lines.
L162: 
L163: #### JSON lines【10†】
L164: 
L165: Several commands, in particular long running ones or those that generate a large output, use a format also known as JSON lines. It consists of a stream of new-line separated JSON messages. You can determine the nature of the message using the `message_type` field.
